[standards/governance/ai/STD-GOV-AI-004-federated-ai-change-control.md#purpose-statement]

### Purpose Statement

This standard provides the controlled, auditable change process for all modifications to enterprise AI agents in the federated delivery model. It defines change type classifications, a tiered approval matrix, required change record fields, and an emergency change path — enabling team autonomy without compromising enterprise stability, auditability, or rollback capability.
page_texts.5:
[standards/governance/ai/STD-GOV-AI-004-federated-ai-change-control.md#scope]

### Scope

This standard applies to all capability, schema, prompt, policy, and lifecycle state changes for AI Agents (Configured) and Custom AI Agents across all teams. It applies at all lifecycle states except Retired. Changes to Retired capabilities require documentation only, not approval review.
page_texts.6:
[standards/governance/ai/STD-GOV-AI-004-federated-ai-change-control.md#compliance-level]

### Compliance Level

Mandatory. No change may be made to a Production agent without a change record.
page_texts.7:
[standards/governance/ai/STD-GOV-AI-004-federated-ai-change-control.md#business-rationale]

### Business Rationale

In a federated environment where many contributors can modify agent prompts, schemas, and configurations simultaneously, uncontrolled changes are the primary source of production regressions, policy drift, and audit failures. A tiered change control process allows routine changes to proceed through domain-level approval while ensuring that high-impact changes receive the appropriate governance review.

[standards/governance/ai/STD-GOV-AI-004-federated-ai-change-control.md#mandatory-requirements]

### Mandatory Requirements

**Change Type Classification:**

Every change to an AI agent must be classified as one of the following types before the approval path is determined:

1. **Metadata change** — changes to agent metadata fields (version, policy classification, tags, description, etc.) that do not affect agent behavior. Owner and backup-owner changes are classified as Type 6 (Ownership or lifecycle state change), not Type 1.
2. **Prompt wording change** — changes to prompt text that affect presentation or wording but do not change the agent's behavioral scope or output schema
3. **Intent scope change** — changes that expand or contract the agent's in-scope or out-of-scope intent definitions
4. **Output schema change** — changes to required fields, required sections, section order, or prohibited content patterns in the output contract
5. **Policy and governance change** — changes to cross-cutting policy instructions, compliance controls, or governance rules applied by the agent
6. **Ownership or lifecycle state change** — changes to the agent's owner assignment or lifecycle state transition
7. **System connection register change** — adding, removing, or modifying a declared system connection, including changes to the connection's identity model, permitted operations, execution mode, or data sensitivity classification

**Approval Matrix:**

| Change Type | Required Approvals |
|---|---|
| Metadata change | Domain owner approval |
| Prompt wording change | Domain owner approval plus Platform Governance Team validation lead |
| Intent scope change | Domain owner approval plus Platform Governance Team review |
| Output schema change | Domain owner approval plus Platform Governance Team review |
| Policy and governance change | Platform Governance Team plus Enterprise Copilot Architecture Board approval |
| Ownership or lifecycle state change | Domain owner approval |
| System connection register change | Domain owner approval plus Platform Governance Team review; add Data and Compliance Owner approval when the change adopts a Service Identity or approves autonomous Write/Action execution (per STD-TEC-AI-008) |
| Lifecycle state promotion | Quality gate sign-off per STD-TEC-AI-005; High-Tech governance review |

**Required Change Record:**

Every change request must include:

1. Requested change — a specific description of what is being changed
2. Business rationale — why this change is needed; the business driver or defect being addressed
3. Risk assessment — the potential for regression, behavioral change, or compliance impact
4. Impacted capabilities and teams — other agents, intents, or teams that may be affected by this change
5. Validation plan — how the change will be tested before release; reference to the scenario suite from STD-TEC-AI-005
6. Rollback plan — how the change will be reversed if it causes regression; including the rollback trigger criteria
7. Approval evidence — the recorded approvals per the approval matrix

**Emergency Change Process:**

When an immediate production change is required due to a compliance incident, critical defect, or platform emergency:

1. Define what constitutes an emergency — criteria must be documented in advance, not determined case by case
2. Follow the expedited approval path — expedited does not mean unapproved; the domain owner must approve at minimum, and the Platform Governance Team must be notified immediately
3. Post-change review within the defined window — typically within three business days; the normal approval matrix applies retrospectively
4. Rollback readiness must be documented before the change is deployed, even under emergency conditions

**Deployment Controls:**

- No direct production edits without a change record — agents must not be modified in their Production configuration without a preceding change record
- Batch related changes — when multiple changes are needed, batching them into a single release reduces regression risk and audit surface
- Validate in representative scenarios before release — every change must be tested against the scenario suite (STD-TEC-AI-005) before deployment
page_texts.10:
[standards/governance/ai/STD-GOV-AI-004-federated-ai-change-control.md#recommended-practices]

### Recommended Practices

- Maintain a change backlog for each domain; triage the backlog weekly to identify changes that can be batched
- Document rollback plans before beginning the change, not after — rollback planning under pressure produces inadequate plans
page_texts.11:
[standards/governance/ai/STD-GOV-AI-004-federated-ai-change-control.md#prohibited-practices]

### Prohibited Practices

- Direct Production modifications without a change record are prohibited regardless of the perceived impact of the change
- Emergency changes without documented rollback readiness may not be deployed
- Prompt changes that affect output schema or agent behavior must not be classified as "wording changes" to bypass the higher approval tier
page_texts.12:
[standards/governance/ai/STD-GOV-AI-004-federated-ai-change-control.md#exceptions-process]

### Exceptions Process

1. Requests to classify a higher-impact change at a lower approval tier require Platform Governance Team approval and a documented risk justification
2. All exceptions are recorded in the capability change log

---
page_texts.15:
[standards/governance/ai/STD-GOV-AI-004-federated-ai-change-control.md#change-record-storage]

#### Change Record Storage

- Change records must be stored in a location accessible to the Platform Governance Team for audit purposes
- Change records may not be deleted; they are retained as audit evidence for the capability's full lifecycle
page_texts.16:
[standards/governance/ai/STD-GOV-AI-004-federated-ai-change-control.md#approval-evidence-format]

#### Approval Evidence Format

- Approval evidence must identify the approver by name or identifier, the date of approval, and the change record it applies to
- Verbal or undocumented approvals do not satisfy the requirement
page_texts.17:
[standards/governance/ai/STD-GOV-AI-004-federated-ai-change-control.md#production-edit-controls]

#### Production Edit Controls

- For configured agents: all configuration changes must be made in a non-Production copy first; the Production configuration is updated only after validation
- For custom agents: all changes must follow the engineering change control process (code review, automated testing) in addition to this standard's approval requirements

---
page_texts.20:
[standards/governance/ai/STD-GOV-AI-004-federated-ai-change-control.md#phase-1-change-record-process-establishment]

#### Phase 1: Change Record Process Establishment

1. Define the emergency change criteria in the governance documentation before any emergency arises
2. Define the change backlog channel and triage cadence for each active capability domain
3. Train domain owners and High-Tech reviewers on the approval matrix
page_texts.21:
[standards/governance/ai/STD-GOV-AI-004-federated-ai-change-control.md#phase-2-active-change-management]

#### Phase 2: Active Change Management

1. For every change to a Production agent: open a change record, classify the change type, and confirm the approval path before making any modification
2. Run validation scenarios after the change and before deployment
3. Document the rollback plan and confirm rollback readiness before deployment
page_texts.22:
[standards/governance/ai/STD-GOV-AI-004-federated-ai-change-control.md#phase-3-change-process-audit]

#### Phase 3: Change Process Audit

1. Conduct a monthly change quality audit: verify that all Production changes in the prior month had complete change records and followed the correct approval path
2. Conduct a quarterly process effectiveness review: assess whether the change type categories and approval matrix are correctly calibrated for the portfolio
page_texts.23:
[standards/governance/ai/STD-GOV-AI-004-federated-ai-change-control.md#validation-criteria]

### Validation Criteria

| Validation Area | Criteria | Verification Method | Evidence Required |
| --------------- | --------- | ------------------- | -------------------- |
| Change record completeness | All 7 required fields present in every change record | Change log audit | Change records |
| Approval compliance | Every change has approval evidence matching the approval matrix | Approval record audit | Approval records |
| No unrecorded production changes | All Production changes correspond to a change record | Registry comparison | Change log vs. production version history |
| Rollback plan presence | Every Production change has a documented rollback plan | Change record review | Rollback plan documents |

---
page_texts.25:
[standards/governance/ai/STD-GOV-AI-004-federated-ai-change-control.md#non-compliance-handling]

### Non-Compliance Handling

- Unrecorded Production change detected: immediate incident review; change must be documented retrospectively
- Missing rollback plan: fail the governance gate; do not release the change
- Repeated process bypass by the same contributor: restrict contributor privileges pending architecture board review
page_texts.26:
[standards/governance/ai/STD-GOV-AI-004-federated-ai-change-control.md#governance-oversight]

### Governance Oversight

- **Standards Owner**: Enterprise Copilot Architecture Board
- **Compliance Manager**: Platform Governance Team (monthly change quality audit; weekly change backlog triage)
- **Governance Body**: Enterprise Copilot Architecture Board (policy and governance change approvals; repeated bypass escalation)
